$description: LANE LR (#282) measurement of the 12 logo SVGs in knowledge/assets/logos/. PROPOSE ONLY — nothing under knowledge/ was touched. Measured 2026-09-17.

defects.what: hexagon-dark-colour.svg and hexagon-light-colour.svg are the same drawing: 5 paths, identical geometry and fills, differing only in one float literal (9.15527e-05 vs 8.58307e-05).
defects.proof: 619 bytes each; sha differs; diff = 1 coordinate token
defects.consequence: Expected, not broken — the colour hexagon has no ground-dependent ink (red chevrons + white infill read on both grounds). Two Figma nodes, one asset. Nothing to re-export; the question is whether the library keeps two.

defects.what: The identifier artwork is absent. viewBox is 0 0 795 85 but ink stops at x=314.2 (39.5% of the canvas). The light twins carry a 5,020-character identifier path filled #333333 reaching x=777; this file has no #333333 path at all.
defects.proof: the #333333 identifier path in masterbrand-identifier-light-colour.svg begins d="M404.468 59V24.296"; clean()'s regex requires <path d="M followed by 3+ digits and fill="white"
defects.consequence: Rendered to a box, it is the plain masterbrand at 40%% scale with 60%% empty space to its right — it is not a different lockup, it is the masterbrand mis-framed.
defects.probableCause: _export-logos.py clean() strips <path d="M-?\d{3,}…" fill="white"/> to remove Figma's white background path. The identifier path is <path d="M404.468…"> — it matches the \d{3,} arm and survives in the light files only because it is filled #333333, not white. On a dark export the identifier is white.
defects.unproven: not reproduced — confirming it needs a FIGMA_TOKEN and a re-export, which this lane does not do
